text:
maria: FYI hit a pretty nasty streaming bug in the wild — clients sometimes see chunks out of order after a disconnect + automatic retry. Got a repro with our hosted API and a tiny proxy sample app.

maria: Repro steps: 1) open EventSource in browser -> connect to /v1/stream 2) simulate flaky network (ctrl+shift+j throttle) 3) disconnect then let SDK retry auth. Observed: some tokens/partials replayed and chunk order stomps on earlier output.

jason: Oof. Which SDK? Node/browser? server side or client polyfill?

maria: Browser EventSource + our node sample that proxies requests (we add auth header). Also saw similar with node-fetch-based SDK in server environment; behavior differs.

li: Quick note: browser EventSource auto-reconnects and uses Last-Event-ID header, fetch streams do not. Our node SDK does a manual reconnect on auth failure and replays the request body which can duplicate chunks unless server is idempotent.

samir: Can you paste minimal proxy code? maybe we're re-sending buffered chunks on reconnect.

maria: Sure — proxy snippet we used:
```js
// express proxy that forwards SSE and adds auth
app.get('/proxy', async (req, res) => {
  const upstream = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream', { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ' + TOKEN } });
  res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'text/event-stream');
  upstream.body.pipe(res); // naive pipe, no handling for upstream close
});
```

maria: When the client disconnects quickly, our app sometimes holds upstream open for a bit (because pipe hasn't handled 'error'/'close') and then reconnect code causes a second upstream connection. Upstream sends chunks, then the original stream finally emits old buffered chunks to the proxy and they get delivered out of order.

emily: Does the API emit chunk sequence numbers? we could rely on that to dedupe / reorder on client.

li: It doesn't today for general streaming. We purposely kept payload minimal. But we have SSE last-event-id support on some endpoints. The parity problem: browser EventSource sets last-event-id automatically for SSEs with id: fields; our node SDK doesn't surface that.

jason: SDK parity + auth retry interplay sounds like root cause: 1) client disconnects 2) SDK retries auth & opens new upstream 3) previous pipe finally flushes buffered chunks 4) proxy forwards both upstream streams to client => out of order/duplicates.

samir: Two mitigations: (A) fix proxy to close upstream immediately on client disconnect and stop piping, (B) add monotonic sequence IDs in chunks from server, (C) SDK should surface reconnect events so user code can handle dedupe.

maria: I tried A — calling upstream.body.cancel() on close mostly worked. But in some environments (older node versions) buffered chunks still flush. Not fully reliable.

emily: B seems robust: server emits `id:` per SSE event or explicit seq in JSON so clients/SDKs can reorder/dedup. Downside: breaking change for some clients if they relied on raw text-only protocol, but we can make seq optional.

li: Agree. Also we should make the Node SDK set/propagate Last-Event-ID on reconnect and provide a `on('reconnect')` hook. That gets closer to EventSource semantics.

jason: For short term: add docs to sample app warning about proxy behavior and show proper cleanup (res.on('close') upstream.body.cancel(), upstream.body.destroy()). For medium term: add seq fields to streaming responses and a small SDK option `streaming.reorder=true` to reorder/dedupe.

deploy-bot: Deployed branch fix/proxy-sse-cleanup to staging (sha: b3c4f1).

maria: Nice. Also logging suggestion: surface http/stream connection ids in traces so we can correlate the two upstream connections that get merged by the proxy.

li: I'll open a GH issue for SDK parity (last-event-id, reconnect hook, reorder option) and a runtime issue to add optional sequence ids to streaming output.

maria: Created a minimal sample PR that demonstrates proper proxy cleanup and shows the client-side dedupe logic using seq numbers. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/samples/pull/42

jason: Thanks — can we add a tiny unit test that simulates a delayed flush from first upstream then a second upstream? would catch regressions.

maria: Yep will add test. Action items: li -> SDK parity GH issue, runtime -> add seq IDs feature flag, maria -> sample PR + test, emily -> add doc note in onboarding guide about proxy pitfalls.

samir: Marking as high priority for devex + eng-runtime.

emily: :thumbsup:
